label: Bioconductor downloads per month
counts: Downloads recorded by Bioconductor for a package in a month.
caveat: Includes CI runs, mirrors and container builds. Read the distinct-IP series instead. The current month is incomplete and is not plotted.

label: Bioconductor distinct IPs per month
counts: Distinct IP addresses downloading a package in a month.
caveat: Closer to people than raw downloads, though it still is not a user count: everyone behind one institutional network collapses into a single address.

label: Bioconductor download rank
counts: Position in Bioconductor's published download score table.
caveat: Worth showing because it comes with a denominator.

label: Registry downloads, all time
counts: The registry's own lifetime download counter, for registries that publish one.
caveat: A running total, never plotted per period. Of the registries here only Bioconductor publishes a lifetime figure. CRAN, npm and PyPI all report a rolling 30-day count instead, which is a different measure and is kept in its own series rather than added to this one. Maven Central publishes no download figure at all.

label: Registry downloads, last 30 days
counts: Downloads in the last 30 days, as reported by registries that publish no lifetime counter.
caveat: A rolling window, not a total, and it moves in both directions: a quiet month is lower than a busy one and that is not an error. Never added to the all-time figures above, which count a different thing over a different period.

label: Registries published to
counts: Distinct registries carrying an artefact built from a department repository.
caveat: Says how many registries carry the software, not how much of it anyone downloads. Found by reverse lookup from the repository URL.

label: Releases per year
counts: A tagged release of a project's repositories, from GitHub Releases and git tags.
caveat: Tags count too. BridgeDb ships as a tag and BridgeDbR ships through Bioconductor, so a Releases-only count misses them.

label: Repositories active in the last year
counts: A project's repositories pushed to in the last 365 days.
caveat: A quiet repository is not a dead one. A finished tool needs no commits.

label: Papers mentioning the software
counts: Works the Research Software Directory records as mentioning a tool.
caveat: Computed by the NL eScience Center rather than here. It counts a tool being named in a paper's text, which is a much weaker signal than a citation, and it misses software that was used without being named at all.

label: Container pulls, all time
counts: Docker Hub's lifetime pull counter for an image.
caveat: One pull is not one user. A CI job rebuilding hourly pulls the base image every time, and a single pull of a multi-arch image can register more than once. Images published only to other registries are missing from this chart.

label: Last release
counts: The date of a project's most recent release or tag.
caveat: Old is not the same as abandoned. ArrayAnalysis has not moved since 2013 and is still cited.

label: Citations of the tool's papers
counts: Citations to every paper describing a tool, summed across its update papers.
caveat: Citing a software paper is not proof the software was used, and these are lifetime counts, so a 2003 paper reflects twenty years. Several of these tools are built by communities far larger than this department, and their citations belong to those communities too.

label: Citations per paper
counts: Citations to one paper, from OpenAlex.
caveat: Every update paper is counted, because people cite whichever was current when they did the work.

label: Packages depending on it
counts: Other published packages that declare a dependency on one of these, as counted by the registry it is published in.
caveat: Counts published packages only, so an analysis script or an unreleased application that depends on a tool is invisible here, and a registry sees only its own: the R packages built on BridgeDb do not appear beside its Maven artefacts. Reported because Maven Central publishes no download figures at all, and this is the number it does keep.
